counterfactual_missing_items: A diagnostic algorithm for dizziness suggested a low probability of central or peripheral vestibular origin
Repeat brain MRI showed no signs of recent vascular lesions
Transcranial Doppler confirmed tortuosity and plaques but demonstrated normal hemodynamics of the cerebro-afferent vessels
decisive_items: recurrent dizzying attacks characterized by sudden subjective vertigo, absence of nausea or vomiting, and unsteadiness with a wide-based gait requiring support
severe dizziness worsened by any movement or position change
she adopted a wide-based stance, was unsteady, and required external supports to walk
response.rationale: R5 best captures the core symptom complex of episodic vertigo, movement/position sensitivity, and unsteadiness with a wide-based gait. R6 only explains the unsteadiness and lacks the vertigo and movement-provoked dizziness. R8, R7, and R3 are contradicted by normal hemodynamics and absent recent vascular lesions; R1 is an incidental chronic imaging finding; R2 lacks cervical-specific findings. The algorithm's low probability of central/peripheral vestibular origin is a partial disconfirmation, but R5 remains the broadest vestibular-pattern match among the supplied candidates.

rejected.why: Contradicted by normal cerebro-afferent hemodynamics, absent recent vascular lesions, and low probability of vestibular origin.
Chronic periventricular white matter changes are non-specific and do not explain episodic vertigo or movement-provoked dizziness.
Carotid stenosis was overestimated and hemodynamics were normal, so atherosclerosis is not the active cause.
No cervical spine findings or neck-specific provocation are present; movement sensitivity is non-specific.
Presumed stroke was not confirmed and repeat MRI showed no recent vascular lesions.
